messages.content: I need to set up Minneapolis for the scholarly publishing conference, Tuesday, April 13 through Friday, April 16. Registration and the reception start at 5:30 Tuesday, and my last meeting ends at noon Friday. Please look at flights from Denver and compare the conference hotel with something less expensive in the Warehouse District.

I’ll keep Tuesday arrival early enough for registration and exclude Friday departures that interfere with the noon meeting. Is this just for you, and do you want to compare nonstop economy flights before looking at the hotels?
Just me, economy. Nonstop would be best for this one, but show me the practical choices rather than the absolute cheapest fare.

Three nonstop combinations fit. Option A leaves Denver Tuesday at 9:05 a.m. and reaches MSP at 11:58 a.m.; the Friday return leaves at 3:20 p.m. and arrives in Denver at 4:36 p.m., for $347 round trip. Option B departs Tuesday at 11:10 a.m., arrives at 2:03 p.m., and returns Friday at 4:55 p.m., landing at 6:14 p.m., for $318. Option C uses the 9:05 a.m. outbound and a 6:35 p.m. Friday return, arriving at 7:52 p.m., for $329. All are currently standard economy fares before any checked-bag or seat charges.
The 11:10 departure looks a little tight. How long should I allow from landing to the conference property downtown?

From MSP, light rail to downtown generally takes about 25 minutes, plus roughly 10 to 20 minutes for waiting and walking from the station. With deplaning and a carry-on, a 2:03 p.m. arrival should put you at the hotel around 3:10 to 3:35. A taxi or rideshare commonly takes 20 to 30 minutes in ordinary traffic, but afternoon congestion can extend that. The later outbound is workable for 5:30 registration, though it leaves less recovery room if the flight is delayed.
Then keep the 9:05 outbound. I don’t need to rush into the reception after a delay. Compare the two Friday returns more carefully.

For the 3:20 p.m. flight, leaving the downtown venue at 12:30 would provide about 35 minutes to retrieve a bag and get underway, with an estimated airport arrival near 1:20 by light rail or somewhat earlier by car. That is adequate but not generous. The 6:35 p.m. flight allows lunch after the meeting and a relaxed airport transfer around 3:30. It also lowers the combined fare by $18, from $347 to $329, when paired with the 9:05 Tuesday departure.
Use the later Friday flight as the working choice. Now the hotels.

The conference property beside the venue has a standard king at $239 nightly. For three nights, taxes and destination charges bring the estimated total to $833. It offers direct indoor access to conference events and can hold your bag Friday after checkout. A Warehouse District hotel has a king at $169 nightly, approximately $589 including taxes for the same three nights. It is about 1.2 miles from the venue: roughly 7 minutes by light rail after the walk to and from stations, 8 to 15 minutes by car, or about 25 minutes on foot.
Does the Warehouse number include parking or any mandatory fee? I won’t have a car.

No parking is included or needed. The $589 estimate includes the hotel’s mandatory $12 nightly facilities charge and lodging taxes. The rate is cancellable until 6:00 p.m. two days before arrival. The conference hotel estimate includes its mandatory destination charge; its conference rate can be canceled without penalty until 72 hours before arrival.
What would I realistically spend getting back and forth from the Warehouse District? Wednesday starts at 9:00, Thursday runs through a 7:00 dinner, and Friday I have the noon meeting.

Using light rail for the conference commute would be about $12 to $15 total across Wednesday through Friday, depending on ticket type and whether the dinner requires an extra ride. Allow 20 to 25 minutes door to door each way, including walking and waiting. Using rideshare for an early Wednesday arrival, Thursday evening return, and Friday with luggage would likely total $45 to $70. That puts the Warehouse hotel at roughly $604 with transit or $634 to $659 with several car trips, still $174 to $229 below the conference property.
Tuesday airport transportation is needed either way, correct? And what about Friday with my suitcase?

Correct. Airport transportation is largely common to both choices. Light rail from MSP is about $2.50 to $3.25 and serves both downtown areas, though each hotel has a different final walk. On Friday, the conference hotel will hold your suitcase after checkout. The Warehouse hotel also confirms same-day luggage storage, but you would need to return there after the noon meeting before heading to MSP. That adds approximately 35 to 50 minutes if you use rail and walking, or about 20 to 30 minutes by car.
That return for the bag is the part I don’t like. Could I bring it to the venue Friday?

The conference registration desk offers supervised luggage storage Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. for registered attendees. You could check out of the Warehouse hotel, take the bag to the venue before the meeting, collect it around 12:15, and continue directly to MSP. That removes the Warehouse District backtrack and still leaves more than five hours before the 6:35 flight.
Good. Is the conference hotel premium doing anything else for me besides proximity?

Its main advantages are immediate access to the Wednesday panel, easy breaks between exhibitor appointments, no exposure to weather during the connected portions, and simpler Thursday dinner logistics. It also gives you more flexibility to return to the room during the day. The Warehouse hotel saves at least about $174 after realistic local travel, but it adds two commutes Wednesday, two Thursday, and one Friday morning.
Put together one sensible plan for each hotel, including when I would leave on Wednesday and Friday.

Conference-property plan: take the Tuesday 9:05 a.m. nonstop, land at 11:58, use light rail or a car downtown, and check in around 1:30. On Wednesday, leave the room by 8:35 for the 9:00 panel. Check out Friday around 8:00, store the bag at the hotel, attend the noon meeting, collect it at 12:20, have lunch, and leave for MSP around 3:30. Estimated air, hotel, and airport transit total: about $1,172. Warehouse plan: use the same flights, check in around 1:30 to 2:00 Tuesday, and leave the hotel by 8:10 Wednesday. On Friday, check out by 8:00, reach the venue by 8:30, deposit the bag at registration, collect it at 12:15, and leave for MSP after lunch around 3:30. Estimated total with light rail for most trips and two rideshares: about $968 to $988.
I’m leaning toward the Warehouse hotel. Is there any concern about getting back there after the publisher dinner Thursday?

The dinner is at the conference property and is expected to finish around 9:00 p.m. Light rail service continues well beyond that hour, and the relevant ride is short. Including the station walks, plan on 20 to 25 minutes. A rideshare should take around 10 minutes and is the more direct fallback if the dinner runs late or conditions are poor.
Let’s narrow it to the 9:05 Tuesday outbound, the 6:35 Friday return, and the Warehouse hotel. Don’t book either one yet. Give me the separate decisions and the deadlines I need to watch.

Working flight choice: nonstop Denver to Minneapolis Tuesday at 9:05 a.m., arriving 11:58 a.m.; nonstop return Friday at 6:35 p.m., arriving Denver at 7:52 p.m. Current round-trip economy fare is $329, unbooked, and can change at any time. Working hotel choice: Warehouse District standard king for three nights, Tuesday through Friday, estimated at $589 including taxes and the mandatory facilities charge. It is also unbooked; free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. local time Sunday, April 11, after which one night plus tax is charged. Plan on about $50 to $70 for all local travel if you combine rail with two rideshares. Friday, take the suitcase to conference registration before the meeting and retrieve it by 2:00 p.m. The flight and hotel remain separate pending decisions.
